overview: A population is one species living together in an area; a community is all the different populations living and interacting together.
genZNote: Population: everyone of the same species in the neighbourhood. Community: the whole neighbourhood, every species included.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: A group of individuals of the same species living in a specific area at the same time.
aspects.valueB: All the populations of different species living and interacting together in a given area.

aspects.label: Scope
aspects.valueB: Multi-species scope, including all their interactions.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: All the deer in a particular forest.
aspects.valueB: All the deer, wolves, trees, and other species together in that same forest.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The ecological hierarchy runs: organism → population → community → ecosystem → biome → biosphere — a frequently tested sequence.
overlay.memoryTrick: Population = one species. Community = many species together.
overlay.commonMisconception: 'Community' in ecology refers only to living organisms — it does not include the non-living (abiotic) environment, which is added in at the ecosystem level.
